speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what mechanisms are in place to ensure that foster carers are able to access all appropriate and relevant health information about the children and young people in their care; and (b) what mechanisms are in place to ensure that the birth parents do not impede access to the health information, including information stored on the Health Buddy app.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua) (for the Minister for Social and Family Development)
text: This letter facilitates communication with healthcare professionals and ensures the child’s medical needs are properly addressed.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: However, foster parents do face delays, especially in healthcare treatment, mainly because of the procedural challenges.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Sometimes, it is temporary, but sometimes, foster children are in the care of the foster parents for a longer period of time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: Under those circumstances, there have been situations where a child's appointment has been cancelled by the natural parents because they have access to the Health Buddy and, because of this delay, sometimes, the child needs to be prepped before he or she goes to the hospital.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: These are some of the challenges that are happening on the ground.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: My question is: can there be more support given via MSF and the Ministry of Health (MOH) in terms of addressing these delays and maybe temporarily preventing the natural parents from having access or cancelling the appointment of their children on Health Hub or Health Buddy?

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: The other thing is whether it is possible to have a dedicated health liaison person that social workers can work with MOH, because some of these children do need a lot of help and foster parents can be running around.

speaker: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim (Nominated Member)
text: So, greater help and greater assistance will be wonderful between the two Ministries.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: So, in terms of getting access to these standard treatments and medication, I do not think the natural parents will be an obstacle to the process.

speaker: Mr Eric Chua
text: What we can do is that we can continually engage foster parents.
